title: Configure call intake, dispatch behavior and closeout
summary: Review call intake, recipient scope, status automation, recommendation tuning, timer rules and form policy, then interpret an actual training closeout.
prerequisites: Use the fictional Chicago Fire training department with department-settings access.
Run-card and conditional-response controls must be available for the recommendation sections.
Know the configured unit status sets, roster and crew assignments before changing automation.
Preserve existing calls, counters, provider configuration and access controls; this walkthrough reviews captured settings and one existing training closeout.

We are reviewing the controls without sending an import or demonstrating an automatic close.

scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
required_labels: Set Status for Shift Personnel On Dispatch
scenes.narration: Open Call & Dispatch Settings. Use Shift for Group Dispatch selects the resolved on-duty roster; an empty roster falls back to group members for notification routing. Set Status for Shift Personnel On Dispatch is a separate switch. Automatic personnel dispatch and release statuses require both switches and use the resolved shift personnel. The two Person Call status controls choose those statuses. Both switches remain off here. Review the actual roster before changing them; an empty notification fallback does not create a shift or establish a status change.

scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
scenes.narration: Group-Scoped Dispatch separates area scope from recipient selection. When Scope Dispatch to Group Areas is enabled, supported views and nearest comparisons follow the member’s group subtree and applicable calls. Department administrators and selected Department-Wide Dispatch Roles retain a wider view. Our scope switch and role exceptions remain off; the operator is a department administrator. Group Boundary defines response areas separately. A unit can remain listed without a nearest comparison, so review scope, status and position together.

scenes.title: Review unit recipients and status targets
scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
scenes.narration: Also Dispatch To Assigned Personnel and Also Dispatch To Entire Group can expand a unit’s notification audience. Both are off here. Unit Call Dispatch Status and Unit Call Release Status are separate meaning-based choices. Defaults resolve within each unit’s own status set; built-in units use Responding on dispatch and Released on release. A missing matching custom status leaves the unit unchanged. Custom-status types can provide type-specific override rows. This Engine type uses Standard Actions, so this example has no such rows. Review crew assignments and status meanings before broadening recipients or changing targets.

required_labels: Personnel on Unit Set Unit Status
scenes.narration: Personnel on Unit Set Unit Status controls linked crew context: a supported unit-status submission can place its submitted crew roles into On Unit. It remains off here. Hold to set status also remains off. When enabled in supported Unit and Responder apps, crews hold a status for two seconds; statuses requiring a note or destination still open that step. Verify that behavior in the app version crews use. These switches do not create crew assignments or establish anyone’s qualification.

scenes.title: Review recommendations and waiting resources
scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
scenes.narration: Run Cards & Automatic Dispatch shows Closest Unit Response with automatic dispatch off. Rest period deprioritizes recently dispatched resources; minimum staffing checks configured seats, and move-up checks station minimums. Our rest period is zero, staffing gate off and move-up off. Closest Unit Response Tuning has 1800-second location ages, a zero radius limit, meaning no maximum, stale locations excluded and routed ETA off. The shortlist is five. Station turnout is 120 seconds; mobile and personnel turnout are zero. Freed-unit automatic dispatch remains off; its limit bounds automatic sends while alerts still occur. Response codes is empty; its name, colour, retirement and crew-display controls apply when codes exist. Review New Call recommendations before sending.

required_labels: Auto-Enable Check-In Timers for New Calls
scenes.narration: Auto-Enable Check-In Timers for New Calls is off. Default Timer Configurations is empty. The saved Investigation Personnel override is 60 minutes, warning five, enabled for all states and any priority. Matching overrides take precedence over defaults; the call’s own timer flag also matters. Our separately enabled training call shows Boden’s timer. No check-in receipt is established here. Timer forms use their own Add controls, and station coverage has a separate Save. Station Coverage Minimums currently has no saved requirements; its station, target, count and radius fields are a preparation form.

scenes.narration: New Call Form Fields has separate Visible and Required columns. Here the optional fields are visible and their required boxes are clear. Name, nature, priority and type always remain required. A missing required value can block a new call, archived-call entry or saved edit; hidden fields cannot remain mandatory. Plus Code is a location-finding aid and cannot be required; require GPS Coordinates when a saved point is necessary. Review both halves of the table, then the corresponding call form. This example preserves the current field policy.

scenes.title: Inspect a real training closeout
scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
scenes.narration: Use the existing training example 26-4. Its Dispatched tab stores Engine 51 and Christopher Herrmann. Stored assignment alone does not confirm device receipt. On its Close Call form, Completed Type is Closed, training notes are entered and Send Notification is off. The saved call then shows Closed with closing details and notes. Release policy moves only units still working that call. Units already back in service, unavailable, under maintenance, on break or working another open call can keep their status. Review status history separately when validating release behavior.

scenes.title: Review automatic closure and apply the policy
scenes.capture_intent: Show the ordered actual views and exact controls in capture_evidence. Preserve disabled/current policy; do not invent an enabled test or saved row.
required_labels: Close call when last unit clears
scenes.narration: Close call when last unit clears is off in this example. If enabled, every dispatched unit must report finished after dispatch; returning or transporting still keeps work open. Calls without dispatched units, future undispatched calls and active incident command retain their closeout guards. This training example uses manual closure. Chicago Fire can review station crews and notification audiences. Community care or mental health teams can review rosters; search and rescue teams availability and qualifications; security teams patrol coverage. Wildland contractors and industrial teams can check crew capability and access. Verify call state, status history and recipient receipt separately.
scenes.practice: Explain the automatic-close guards and choose a controlled verification plan suited to your sector.
